architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept realization-state control as adequate for a subsequent level comparison if S_max is less than or equal to 100.0%, equivalently if the largest max/min viscosity ratio across the three preparations at 120 or 130 C is less than or equal to 2.00.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The observable is measured directly on three preparations of the resin-modified S1C41 chemistry over 80-130 C, including 120 and 130 C. It therefore stays inside the measured chemistry and temperature support of this experiment. The primary observable does not depend on a rheological regularity previously measured in the same chemistry family, nor does it transfer the unmodified-family shared thermal shape; any fitted viscosity-scale coordinate is derived from the repeated S1C41 sweeps themselves. The result supports only a formulation-level assessment of realization reproducibility, not a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If S_max is greater than 100.0%, equivalently if either the 120 C or 130 C max/min ratio exceeds 2.00, falsify the operational hypothesis that the present preparation protocol controls realization state adequately for formulation-level discrimination. If S_max is less than or equal to 100.0%, that operational hypothesis is not falsified. Neither outcome by itself falsifies H-LEVEL-DILUTE, H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC, because this card contains no contemporaneous unmodified E2 comparator and therefore cannot produce their required relative level change.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Tighten and fully record the preparation history and repeat S1C41::M-REPEAT until S_max is less than or equal to 100.0%. After state control is demonstrated, run S1C41::M-SWEEP with contemporaneous process-history-matched unmodified E2 preparations and use paired 120 and 130 C relative changes to test the three registered level predictions.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Maximum between-preparation viscosity-scale spread at the decision temperatures, S_max = max over T in {120, 130 C} of 100 * [max_j eta_j(T) / min_j eta_j(T) - 1], using the three independently prepared S1C41 sweeps.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41::M-REPEAT is the scientifically defensible prerequisite to interpreting any modifier-level comparison. It directly tests whether preparation-state variability is reduced below a numeric 2.00-fold limit, avoids unsupported shared-shape transfer, and prevents a realization displacement from being misclassified as support for one of the three formulation-level hypotheses.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: The Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator preferred S1C41::M-SWEEP based on deterministic VOI and minimum modifier burden. I follow the Skeptic on the decisive protocol issue: that card measures only one candidate preparation and lacks the contemporaneous unmodified E2 reference required for its stated relative-change observable, while the proposed 3.40% threshold is not credible against the historical 2.80-3.57-fold E2 spread. Rather than claim unattainable hypothesis falsification, I depart from the deterministic ranking and select the available S1C41 state-control card. The binding chemistry audit permits M-REPEAT because it directly observes the modified chemistry.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: No prior local repeatability data exist for AC1920/TK100-modified chemistry, and the external-prior queries returned no rows. This experiment supplies candidate-specific repeatability evidence but does not isolate AC1920, TK100, or their interaction.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: S1C41 uses 15% acrylic-like and 5% tackifier-like loading within the stated supported regions, and all temperatures are directly measured between 80 and 130 C. No unmodified-family shape transfer or temperature extrapolation is used.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: Viscosity is measured directly at 120 and 130 C within an 80-130 C sweep. The decision uses the catalogued 100.0% state-control threshold rather than the 3.40% shared-shape fit residual, which is not a demonstrated paired-comparison resolution.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: This is the dominant uncertainty and is directly estimated from three independent preparations. Three preparations provide only a coarse bound on the distribution, but they are materially more informative than the single preparation in M-SWEEP.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local shared temperature-response regularity was measured in the original reactive-PUR chemistry represented by E1, E2, and E3; the E1 +P chemical perturbation is a separate compatibility check rather than part of the primary same-composition fit. A discriminating experiment requires a nonzero acrylic-like and/or minor-tackifier-like modifier on the E2 reactive core, so it changes chemistry and cannot be assumed to remain inside the measured support. Shared-shape transfer must be audited for the specific candidate; absent affirmative support, the experiment should use a direct 80-130 C sweep rather than one-point reconstruction.
planner.failure_mode: Uncontrolled displacement of the realized viscosity level, creating a risk that a modified formulation will fall outside the processing-viscosity window at 120-130 C.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: For E2, nominal runs differ by max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57 across 80-130 C, with sample CV values of 0.46-0.58. This measured spread establishes large realization/process-state uncertainty; whether any proposed modified candidate is inside the processing window remains unmeasured.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Temperature response has six-point sweeps from 80 to 130 C for multiple original formulations and runs, and realized-level variability is quantified for three E2 runs. In contrast, the isothermal evidence consists only of single four-point 120 C trajectories for E1 and E5 over 15-90 min. Their measured drifts differ substantially: E1 changes by 9.51% from 15 to 60 min and 16.85% from 15 to 90 min, whereas E5 changes by 51.54% and 93.08%, respectively. There are no replicated hold trajectories, no E2 hold, and no hold data for a modified candidate.
measurement_requirements: Use a nonzero modifier loading, because the unmodified reactive-core option gives no differential prediction and cannot separate the registered level hypotheses.
Measure viscosity directly at 120 and 130 C, or obtain those points within a direct 80-130 C sweep, without extrapolating beyond measured temperature support.
Include a matched unmodified E2-core reference prepared under the same recorded process history so modifier effects can be separated from realization-state displacement.

Use independent preparations or otherwise quantify repeatability, because the measured E2 run spread of 2.80-3.57-fold is larger than the declared 3.4% sweep and 8.8% anchor discrimination thresholds.
Compare the measured level change prospectively against the frozen inert-dilution, acrylic-elevation, and plasticization predictions using the applicable measurement-resolution threshold.
Verify the temperature-response shape directly for chemistry-changing modifiers unless the chemistry applicability audit supports one-point state calibration.
Add a replicated 120 C hold with measurements at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min if the experiment is also expected to resolve residence-time stability; report SI_15_60 without imputing later times.
planner.scientific_question: At matched process state and 120-130 C, does a nonzero-modifier E2-core formulation have a realized viscosity level consistent with inert-dilution tracking, measurably above that prediction as specified by H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or measurably below it as specified by H-LEVEL-PLASTIC?

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry outside the family in which the shared thermal-response shape was established. However, M-SWEEP directly measures the decision-temperature viscosity and establishes the response shape for this candidate rather than transferring the unmodified-family shape, so it is admissible under the binding audit. Its 15% acrylic-like and 5% minor-tackifier-like loadings are within the stated supported regions, including the conservative 15-20% acrylic band and repeated 4.8-6.4% minor-resin cluster.
hypotheses_not_separated: None among the three registered level hypotheses; thermal-hold drift hypotheses are not tested by M-SWEEP.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: A 120-130 C level change within 3.40% of exactly one prediction accepts that formulation-level prediction for S1C41: -42.76% supports H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% supports H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or -72.76% supports H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. This does not establish a molecular mechanism or thermal-hold stability.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: A result at or below -42.76% falsifies H-LEVEL-ASSOC; a result at or above -42.76% falsifies H-LEVEL-PLASTIC; and departure from -42.76% by more than the 3.40% sweep resolution falsifies H-LEVEL-DILUTE. Thus an outcome can falsify the dilution prediction even if it does not land within resolution of either alternative prediction.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: If the result is not within 3.40% of exactly one registered prediction, no hypothesis is accepted for this composition. Such a result would indicate unregistered behavior, insufficient process-state matching, or realization variability; the large historical E2 run spread would then motivate state-controlled replication rather than post hoc assignment.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level across 80-130 C, especially the 120 and 130 C level change relative to the unmodified reactive core; the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T is secondary.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Tied in deterministic VOI and fully supported, but its 17.5% acrylic loading creates a larger chemistry perturbation than S1C41 without separating additional hypothesis pairs.
Tied in deterministic VOI and has a directly commensurate 20% acrylic evidence anchor, but carries greater total modifier burden than the smallest sufficient tied design.
Tied in deterministic VOI but uses 22.5% acrylic, increasing departure from the characterized reactive chemistry without added discrimination.
Tied in deterministic VOI and remains inside the broad supported region, but its 25% acrylic loading is the largest perturbation in the tied set and lies outside the conservative initial 15-20% band.
It separates all three pairs directly, but its 7.5% tackifier loading lies above the repeated 4.8-6.4% evidence cluster, creating a nonzero extrapolation penalty and a lower VOI score.

proposer.reasoning: S1C41::M-SWEEP has the maximum VOI score of 0.6875, directly measures the processing-window level at 120 and 130 C, and separates all three registered hypothesis pairs at 3.40% resolution. Unlike an inadmissible one-point anchor for modified chemistry, it does not assume transfer of the unmodified-family thermal shape. The remaining limitation is moderate process-state risk: the sweep does not itself control preparation variability, so interpretation requires a matched unmodified reference and careful process-history matching.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards directly separate all three hypothesis pairs with identical VOI components and no extrapolation penalty. S1C41 uses the smallest total modifier burden, 15% AC1920 plus 5% TK100, while remaining inside both supported intervention regions. This follows the declared policy to prefer the smallest sufficient departure from characterized chemistry when evidence coverage and interpretability are otherwise comparable.

residual_decision_risk: The catalogued card contains only one fresh candidate preparation and no contemporaneous process-history-matched unmodified E2 reference, so the primary relative-change observable is not operationally obtained.
The 3.40% sweep-fit residual is not demonstrated paired-comparison resolution under the large historical E2 realization variability.
Without matched replication, preparation-state displacement may be mistaken for a modifier-dependent formulation effect.
The dual-axis formulation leaves AC1920-specific, TK100-specific, and interaction effects entangled; only combined formulation-level behavior can be assessed.
M-SWEEP does not resolve thermal-hold drift or hot-residence-time stability.
The small 0.002292 VOI margin means untested weight regimes outside the reported 0.5-1.5 scaling sweep could alter the deterministic ranking.

The modified chemistry has not previously demonstrated transferable thermal-response shape; this sweep verifies S1C41 directly but does not by itself authorize future M-ANCHOR use without a versioned transferability determination.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection does not identify another available card that can produce the required matched S1C41-versus-unmodified-E2 comparison with adequate state control. S1C41::M-SWEEP remains the appropriate available direct measurement for the modified chemistry and verifies its 80-130 C response. However, as catalogued, its single-preparation protocol lacks a contemporaneous matched E2 reference and cannot justify the nominal 3.40% formulation-comparison threshold against the documented 2.80-3.57-fold E2 run spread. Therefore its result may establish the candidate's absolute viscosity-temperature curve and chemistry-specific response shape, but it cannot validly accept or falsify the three formulation-level hypotheses from the relative-change boundaries. Matched E2 controls and independent paired preparations are required before making those comparisons. The dual-axis intervention also cannot attribute an observed effect specifically to AC1920, TK100, or their interaction, although that does not distinguish among the five tied cards because all use the same dual-axis structure.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The tied top set is unchanged in all 29 reported scenarios: top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, and every weight term survives independent scaling from 0.5 to 1.5 with no recommendation_flip_boundary. Thus no tested perturbation causes S1C41::M-SWEEP or the five-card tied top set to cease being top ranked. The base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower is only 0.002292, so untested weightings outside the sweep could matter, but the payload provides no scientific basis for preferring such weightings.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary observable stays within measured support because S1C41::M-SWEEP directly measures the modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry from 80 to 130 C, including 120 and 130 C, and does not transfer the unmodified-family thermal shape. The direct sweep is the required verification for this new chemistry. Future use of M-ANCHOR for this chemistry would require a versioned direct-sweep demonstration of shape transferability.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The stated numerical outcomes could occur, but the protocol as specified cannot generate the matched S1C41-versus-unmodified-E2 percentage change to which the thresholds apply. A single unreplicated candidate sweep also cannot support the declared 3.40% practical resolution against the documented E2 process-state spread. Therefore the criterion is not operationally attainable as a formulation-level falsification criterion without adding a matched reference and replication.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The claimed separation and acceptance of H-LEVEL-DILUTE, H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC could instead reflect preparation-state displacement rather than the modifier-dependent viscosity level.
objections.objection: The three predictions for S1C41 are nominally well separated (-42.76%, 17.24%, and -72.76%), with every pair differing by more than the declared 3.40% M-SWEEP threshold. However, that 3.40% is a shared-shape/intercept-fit residual, not the demonstrated resolution of an unreplicated candidate-versus-reference comparison. The proposed M-SWEEP has min_repeats = 1, does not control process state, and is being interpreted against historical E2 runs whose CV is 0.54-0.58 and max/min ratio is 3.34-3.57 at 120-130 C. Thus the experiment has not established that it can distinguish formulation effects at 3.40% under the stated protocol.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Modifier-specific attribution, additivity, interaction, and any acrylic-association or two-resin plasticization mechanism would remain unsupported even if one formulation-level prediction matches.
objections.objection: S1C41 simultaneously introduces 15% AC1920 and 5% TK100 while reducing the reactive-core fraction to 0.80. The frozen formulation-level predictions remain numerically distinguishable, but this dual-axis intervention cannot isolate an AC1920-specific effect from a TK100-specific effect or an interaction between them. In particular, an elevation above the inert-dilution prediction cannot be attributed specifically to the acrylic-like axis, and a depression below it cannot establish that both modifier axes form the proposed plasticizing continuum.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The reported percentage change cannot be treated as a directly measured matched-state quantity, so comparison with the three registered percentage predictions is uninterpretable.
objections.objection: M-SWEEP directly measures the candidate viscosity at 120 and 130 C, and the fitted E_eta descriptor is correctly secondary. However, the actual decision observable is stated as the 120-130 C level change relative to an unmodified reactive core. The catalog protocol only says to sweep one freshly prepared sample and does not include the matched unmodified E2-core preparation required to calculate that relative change. A historical E2 value would be an unmatched or imputed comparator and is especially unsuitable given the measured 2.80-3.57-fold E2 run spread.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: None for the primary 120-130 C level measurement; only an attempt to replace the sweep with an unverified one-point anchor would invalidate the chemistry-support claim.
objections.objection: No chemistry-domain violation is present in the selected measurement. S1C41 is outside the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family, but M-SWEEP measures 80-130 C directly and verifies the candidate-specific response rather than reconstructing 120-130 C from the unmodified-family shared shape. The proposal does not reuse that shape outside its measured support.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A nominally falsifying result would not constitute practical falsification of a registered formulation-level hypothesis.
objections.objection: The numerical falsification boundaries are in principle reachable by viscosity measurements, but the specified protocol cannot produce the required level change against a matched unmodified core because it includes only one S1C41 sweep. It also supplies no independent preparations capable of demonstrating the claimed 3.40% comparison resolution. Consequently, departure from -42.76% by more than 3.40%, or crossing the -42.76% boundary for H-LEVEL-ASSOC or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC, cannot be assigned to formulation rather than process-state mismatch under this protocol.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No additional unsupported claim follows, provided the interpretation remains restricted to viscosity level and does not relabel a directional level result as proof of molecular association, plasticization, or hot-hold stability.
objections.objection: No unmeasured target outcome is visibly used in the selected experiment or its numerical predictions. The proposer also explicitly limits the result to formulation-level rheology and states that M-SWEEP does not establish a molecular mechanism or thermal-hold stability. The post-validation formalization history is disclosed, and the payload states that validation identity and outcome were excluded from ranking.

skeptic.recommended_change: Run contemporaneous, process-history-matched 80-130 C sweeps for both S1C41 and the unmodified E2 core, using at least three independent preparations per composition with randomized or paired preparation order. Predefine the 120 and 130 C relative-change calculation and base discrimination on the observed paired-comparison uncertainty rather than the 3.40% shared-shape fit residual. If modifier-axis attribution is intended, add separate acrylic-only and tackifier-only controls; otherwise retain the explicit limitation that the dual-axis experiment tests only the combined formulation-level predictions.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The protocol does not include the contemporaneous matched unmodified E2-core sweep needed to calculate its primary relative-change observable, while relying on a 3.40% discrimination threshold despite historical E2 variability of 2.80-3.57-fold and only one planned preparation.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This mandatory upstream audit must be loaded before candidate or experiment ranking so the chemistry provenance, shared-shape evidence, state-shift check, one-point calibration error, original hold contrast, and separate E1 +P perturbation are evaluated on an admissible basis.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

measurement_plan.protocol: Measure viscosity from 80 to 130 C in 10 C increments on a freshly prepared sample and regress ln(eta) against 1/T.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: The measured 120-130 C level change against the unmodified reactive core falls within 3.40% of exactly one registered prediction: -47.12% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 12.88% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC or -80.87% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. That hypothesis is accepted for this composition and the processing-window level is reported with it.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: The 80-130 C sweep is the direct verification measurement that establishes the thermal-response shape for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

budget_efficiency_detail.definition: 1 - effort_points / max(effort_points) over the declared catalog

top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the measured level change is at or below the inert-dilution prediction of -47.12%. H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if it is at or above that same prediction. H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured level change departs from -47.12% by more than the 3.40% resolution of this plan.
